user.title: How is the Sherpa connected?
user.description: The integration reads the unit. Writes stay off unless you turn them on in its options, and even then only parameters the write check has verified on this unit can be changed. RS-485 allows one master, so stop anything else that polls the Sherpa (an old `modbus:` configuration, another controller) before adding it.

init.title: Link, writes and mode control
init.description: The RS-485 link stalls for 10-30 s now and then; that is normal. Entities keep their last values until a failure has lasted as long as set here.

data_description.allow_writes: Off by default. When on, a setpoint becomes writable only after the write check (the Verify write action) has passed for it on this unit. The unit's own controller still runs the plant.
data_description.mode_control: Set the unit's mode from Home Assistant (select, ECO and night switches, climate, hot water), through register 106. Needs Allow writes. Works only while the panel has handed control to RS-485 (ADDR220 = 1): the integration then writes the mode every 60 s, because the unit raises E09 after 255 s without a write. It never writes ADDR220. To hand control back, set ADDR220 = 0 on the panel.

error.mode_control_needs_writes: Mode control needs Allow writes. Turn that on too.

verify_write.name: Verify write
verify_write.description: Checks that one parameter can be written on this unit: writes its own value back, then one step away (held, then read again), and always restores the original. Needs 'Allow writes' on. Admin only.

read_registers.description: Reads raw holding registers through the integration's own connection, for research and support. Without an address it reads every register the unit is known to answer. Only reads, never writes. Admin only.

write_mode_command.name: Write mode command
write_mode_command.description: Research: writes the mode command (register 106), then reads it back with the unit's status, outputs and alarms. The unit acts on it only with ADDR220 = 1, and then raises E09 unless it is written at least every 255 s. Needs 'Allow writes'. Refused while Mode control is on and ADDR220 = 1: turn Mode control off first. Admin only.

unsupported_model.title: Unsupported Sherpa model
unsupported_model.description: The unit reports identify code {code} ({model}). This integration has a register map only for identify code 1134 (Sherpa S2, firmware 0.57), and reading another layout with it would show wrong values. Capture this unit with tools/probe_sherpa.py and open an issue with the result.

restore_failed.title: A Sherpa parameter was left changed
restore_failed.description: The write check could not put {key} (register {address}) back to {value}. Set it on the unit's SERVICE screen, then dismiss this.

serial_control_unmanaged.title: The Sherpa takes commands over RS-485, but nothing keeps it fed
serial_control_unmanaged.description: The unit has ADDR220 = 1 (serial control), and Home Assistant is not writing its mode: Mode control or Allow writes is off. The unit raises E09 every 255 s and stops the pump for about 3 s each time. Set ADDR220 = 0 on the panel, or turn on Allow writes and Mode control in the options.

mode_keepalive_lost.title: Home Assistant is not writing the Sherpa's mode
mode_keepalive_lost.description: The mode has not been written for {seconds} s. The unit pulses its alarm relay (E09) and stops the pump for about 3 s every 255 s. Check the RS-485 link. If it lasts, set ADDR220 = 0 on the panel.

mode_not_applied.title: The Sherpa does not hold the mode we write
mode_not_applied.description: Register 106 reads back something other than what Home Assistant wrote, several times in a row. Another master may be writing it, or the unit refuses it. Check the bus; if it lasts, set ADDR220 = 0 on the panel.
